definition: In models such as transformers, masking involves hiding certain elements of the input from the model; this is a critical part of training language models to handle arbitrary input sequences efficiently.
details: In models such as transformers, masking involves hiding certain elements of the input from the model; this is a critical part of training language models to handle arbitrary input sequences efficiently.

explainer.lead: In transformer-style models, masking hides certain input elements from the model. It matters because masking lets language models handle arbitrary input sequences efficiently during training.

tiers.eli5: It's like covering parts of a page so the model can only work with what it's allowed to see.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply masks in transformers to control which positions the model may attend to when training on arbitrary sequences. A pitfall is that an incorrect mask leaks information the model should not see or blocks context it needs.
tiers.paperLevel: Masking hides certain elements of the input from the model, a critical part of training language models to handle arbitrary input sequences efficiently. Details are tied to the model architecture rather than expressed as a standalone formula.

explainer.example: A sequence of variable length is padded and a mask marks the padding so the model ignores those positions during attention.
